messages:
maria: Kickoff: we need to finalize the Observe roadmap slice for dashboards + tracing hooks this week. Main question: ship higher-fidelity cost attribution now (long lead backend work) or ship templated dashboards + surface-level "estimated cost" and iterate?

raf: My pov: shipping templated dashboards + clear "estimated" labeling gets us into customers' hands fast. High-fidelity cost work should be a separate investment with clear product ROI.

sasha: Agreed but two enterprise prospects asked explicitly for per-model cost SLA export. If we delay, sales will push for an early patch. We should define a gated path: pilot = estimated; pro = reconciled.

lee: Implementation constraints: high-fidelity requires correlating batching and prefix-cache across requests which needs a nightly reconcile job plus token-attribution hooks on the runtime. That's a 4-sprint chunk.

xi: Technically feasible but non-trivial. Proposal: Phase 1 (2 sprints): templates + sampled trace hooks exposing model_route, request_id, sample_pct header, and an "est_cost" metric. Phase 2 (4 sprints): reconciliation job + exportable CSV/S3 + optional 90-day retention.

maria: Good. Let's make concrete gating + rollback criteria for Phase 1 canary so infra knows when to halt rollout.

raf: Canary success metrics (Phase 1):
- Adoption: at least 2 customers instantiate template and run queries.
- Accuracy tolerance: mean per-route delta vs billing < 20% (label as estimated).
- Reliability: median latency increase < 10ms on P95 paths after trace hook enabled.
- No PII logged (automated scrubber on sampled traces).

sasha: Rollback triggers:
- >20% regression in median latency or >3% increase in error-rate within 1 hour after rollout.
- Any sampled traces containing raw prompt content flagged by scrubber.
- Billing delta > 50% for any tenant and unresolved after reconcile run.

lee: Canary config suggestion: start at 1% of tenant traffic for 24h, then 10% for 24h, then 100% if green. Use `hash(tenant_id) % 100 < N` for deterministic ramp.

ops-bot: Canary schedule created: observe-canary-1749954321 at 01:00 UTC. Alerts wired to #eng-oncall and #product. Link: https://ci.internal/canaries/1749954321

xi: One more technical note: we will emit a `trace.sample.meta` field with `batching_hint` and `kv_cache_hit` booleans. That will help post-hoc reconciliation. Need to check storage size impact.

maria: For product copy: display cost as "Estimated cost per route (based on sampled traces)" and link to docs: "How to interpret estimated costs and why batching matters." Add a reconcile button: runs `jobs/reconcile_costs.sh --tenant $T` and shows last-run delta.

raf: Sales action: I'll update playbook to offer "Pro Cost Export" as a paid add-on (requires Phase 2 work and S3 export). Will coordinate with legal on retention/NDA terms.

lee: Designer ask: small UX change to templates: show a yellow info pill when cost is estimated with tooltip text. Can design finish in 3 days?

sasha: I'll own acceptance checklist. Quick items to include:
- Template instantiation flows (3 tenants)
- Reconcile job can be triggered from UI and produces CSV
- Sampled traces include `model_route` + `request_id` and pass PII scrubber tests
- Canary gate metrics > thresholds

maria: Action items:
- Xi: PR for header + `trace.sample.meta` fields, include scrubber integration (due Wed).
- Lee: mockups for yellow pill + reconcile button (3 days).
- Sasha: draft acceptance checklist and post to Confluence.
- Raf: sales play + legal check on export/retention.
- Ops-bot: ensure canary alerts route to oncall and product.

maria: If we agree, I'll lock Phase 1 scope as templates + sampled trace hooks + estimated cost + reconcile button & canary gating. Phase 2 will be explicit "Pro Cost" export + reconciliation automation + longer retention.

raf: Fine by me. Flagging one more risk: customers may treat "estimated" numbers as ground truth; we must make the reconcile flow visible and easy.

xi: Noted. I'll include a reconcile status badge in the UI that shows last reconciliation timestamp and delta.
